correctness.rationale: An explicit natural PL identification of H-fixed points with the union-of-matching-edge-orbit simplicial complex is proved from barycentric coordinates. Exact subgroup generation yields 56 representatives and 1,455 distinct groups and checks every conjugacy count using normalizer orders. The standalone certificate lists elementary free-codimension-one face collapses that are independently replayed on every representative, with all final homotopy types determined by residual graphs or isolated vertices. All 1,455 subgroups are separately reclassified, and an independent barycentric-invariant-face Euler/component calculation checks each representative.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The cycle-type theorem covers all cyclic H in all K_n, and the involution theorem covers one order-two generator: these are acknowledged overlaps but do not quantify over noncyclic subgroups. The arbitrary-subgroup line-clique theorem is for a different face condition (pairwise intersecting rather than disjoint edges). No inspected stronger same-object all-H theorem covers this six-label census.

originality.rationale: The new statement classifies all 1,455 geometric fixed loci for the natural S6-action, including noncyclic subgroups and exact multiplicities. The closest same-object published results quantify over individual cyclic permutations or involutions, while the only inspected arbitrary-subgroup theorem concerns a different complex. Neither the ordinary homology/character nor the cyclic fixed-space homotopy types imply simultaneous noncyclic fixed loci. Searches using exact object, aliases, subgroup parameters, and invariant counts returned no covering classification; priority remains conditional on unindexed literature.

value.rationale: The natural full permutation action on M(K6) has a complete finite fixed-space diagram: an entire canonical six-label group action is classified, rather than a chosen arbitrary slice. Its unexpected rigidity (all nontrivial fixed spaces are collapsible, three points, or empty) and the order-nine example where two three-point cyclic fixed spaces have empty common fixed locus provide genuine structural equivariant information missing from ordinary homology and single-permutation fixed types. The theorem is explicitly finite and not represented as a family theorem.
